lastText: The Case Is ClosedThe Net ClosesNew Ending Discovered · 1 / 16NAPOLEON OF CRIME TAKEN AT LAST: PROFESSOR MORIARTY IN CUSTODYThe trial at the Old Bailey lasts eleven days. Professor Moriarty stands in the dock with his hands folded, a tall, patient, scholarly figure, and listens to the whole of it with the attentive politeness of a man at a lecture. When the verdict is read he inclines his head, as if to a colleague whose argument he had expected. The sentence is penal servitude for life. In the weeks that follow, the network that took ten years to build falls into pieces, and a hundred small crimes across London simply stop. Lestrade shakes your hand on the steps of the court. 'I'll not say I understood it,' he says. 'But I'll say it was done right.' He is remembered as a mind, rather than a man: a machine for solving.
